messages:
maya: Quick summary from the int4 bring-up run: A/B shows a small but measurable MRR dip on longdocs. Thinking we should try a 'metric-ratcheting' rollout instead of the usual fixed-threshold canary. Details below.

cheng: Can you paste the numbers and slices?

maya: Sure — aggregated: baseline v2 MRR=0.4213, candidate int4 MRR=0.4168, delta = -1.08% (45k vs 45k requests, p=0.03). Latency P95: baseline 410ms -> int4 290ms. Cost/token ~ -28%.

lorna: Longdoc slice? that's where we usually see bigger regressions.

maya: longdoc (>2k tokens) slice: baseline 0.374 -> candidate 0.363, delta -2.95% (n=6.8k requests). Shorter contexts near parity.

sam: is KV-cache warmup accounted for? cold starts hit longdocs heavier.

maya: test had mixed warm/cold; we saw longer cold-paths in the longdocs which is consistent with quantized attention scheduling. We also ran a shadowed kv-warmup run and that reduced the longdoc gap by ~0.8 percentage points.

cheng: So there's a measurable customer-visible delta on a heavy slice but big wins on p95 and cost. Metric tradeoff. What's the proposed rollout?

maya: Proposal: metric-ratcheting rollout flow — allow a slightly relaxed canary tolerance at initial low traffic, then progressively tighten over a stability window as sample counts grow and kv cache stabilizes. Auto-fallback still triggers on persistent degradation. Config sketch:

```
# metric-ratcheting canary (pseudo-yaml)
canary:
  steps:
    - traffic: 1%
      duration: 30m
      mrr_tolerance_rel: -2.5%   # initial relaxed tolerance for known longdoc cold bias
    - traffic: 5%
      duration: 2h
      mrr_tolerance_rel: -1.2%
    - traffic: 20%
      duration: 6h
      mrr_tolerance_rel: -0.5%   # final tightened gate before full promote
auto_fallback:
  window: 15m
  condition: delta_mrr_rel <= -1.0% AND p_value <= 0.01
  immediate_rollback: true
post_promote_ratcheting:
  grace_period: 24h
  tighten_to: -0.3%
```

lorna: I like the staged approach. Two questions: 1) why allow -2.5% initially? that seems big. 2) how do we avoid noise-driven flips?

maya: 1) We only allow that at 1% traffic and short window to let the KV warm and for the small longdoc sample to accumulate without killing the run. 2) Use both minimum sample counts per slice and a shrink-wrapped p-value + effect-size rule. Also add a mute period (no auto-promote/rollback) during the first 10m of each step to avoid churn.

cheng: Can we add a slice-aware floor so longdocs need higher sample counts before influencing decisions? e.g., require n>=1k per slice per step.

maya: Yes — the canary checks will include per-slice min_n and a weight cap so a single slice can't veto the whole run unless the effect is both large and statistically significant.

sam: Ops question: will this be supported by the rollout engine? we need to be able to express the ratcheting and the per-slice min_n.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout job created: job_id=rwd-int4-1729473621, cluster=dedicated-canary. Initial 1% step queued.

devops-bot: metrics-bot: A/B dashboard: https://dash.redwood.io/ab/rwd-int4-1729473621 (auto updates every 60s)

lorna: If the dashboard updates every minute we should also add an alert rule for sustained delta to avoid manual chasing. Suggest alert if delta_mrr_rel <= -0.8% for >30m with p<=0.05.

maya: added that to the playbook draft. Also adding an explicit shadow warmup: run 5k longdoc shadow requests with int4 kv warmed before step 2.

cheng: OK. One more: are we going to run a targeted rerank eval? the longdocs may have slightly different ngrams distribution that hits quantization.

maya: Good call. I've queued a rerank set (seeded from customer logs) against both models. Preliminary outputs show difference concentrated on few tokens at passage boundaries. I'll post the diff sample in the runbook.

sam: Operational ask: make rollback quick and safe — snapshot routing and pin fallback to fp16 variant in case the int4 binary has pathologically bad tails.

maya: Yep — fallback policy is to route to fp16-v2 until canary is paused. We'll also record the pre-promote route snapshot in the job metadata.

lorna: If all goes well we'll tighten ratchet to -0.3% after 24h and then promote. If the longdoc slice remains -2% we auto-rollback on the 20% step.

maya: Next steps I already took: 1) created canary job (see job_id above) 2) updated playbook with ratcheting config 3) queued rerank eval 4) added alert rule. I'll post a short retrospective after 24h window.

cheng: Thanks. tagging @platform-team to make sure rollout engine can express the pseudo-yaml.

sam: :thumbsup: keep us posted on early signals.

maya: will do — thanks team.
